source_name: SMIDA — NSSMC issuer disclosure database (річна інформація емітента)
why_relevant: Ukrainian banks are joint-stock issuers and must file regular annual disclosure (річна інформація емітента) with the NSSMC. SMIDA retains the FULL history of a given issuer's filings independently of the bank's own website — so it preserves pre-2022 annual reports of banks whose IR pages are gone. Per-issuer 'showform' URLs are stable and machine-addressable.

source_name: NBU Annual Reports PDF series (admin_uploads direct-file mirror)
why_relevant: NBU annual reports are served as flat, predictably-named PDFs under /admin_uploads/article/, which makes them trivially mirrorable offline and trivially recoverable from Wayback when the CMS reshuffles its navigation. The sector-level baseline document set (incl. 2021 pre-invasion) for this cell's offline-PDF mirror.

source_name: PUMB / FUIB — Financial statements and annual reports archive (bilingual IR)
why_relevant: Best-practice private-bank IR archive in Ukraine with a mirrored EN section and a multi-year back-run of quarterly/annual PDFs. Serves as the reference case for what a full commercial-bank IR archive looks like, and as a high-value target for pre-2022 snapshotting before any future takedown.

source_name: data.gov.ua — NBU organisation datasets (open-data mirror of banking statistics)
why_relevant: State open-data portal carries versioned NBU banking datasets with historical revisions. Because CKAN keeps prior resource versions and the files are flat CSV/XLSX, it is an alternative recovery route for pre-2022 bank-level indicators when the NBU statistics pages are restructured.

source_name: Center for Financial Stability — mirrored NBU Financial Stability/Annual report PDFs
why_relevant: Concrete example of a third-party OFFLINE PDF MIRROR: a US think tank hosting an NBU 2014 annual report copy. Third-party mirrors of central-bank reports are exactly the fallback this cell exists to catalogue, since they are unaffected by .ua hosting disruption.

source_name: NBU resolution/legal-act corpus on relocation and occupied-territory operations (zakon.rada.gov.ua + bank.gov.ua drafts)
why_relevant: The legal trail that explains WHY a channel went dark: NBU Resolution No. 94 on bank activity in combat/occupied/blockaded communities permits suspension of branches; related NBU clarifications cover clients registered on occupied territory. zakon.rada.gov.ua keeps every historical redaction of each act, so it is itself an archive of the regulatory state at any past date.

source_name: Wikipedia (en/uk) bank articles as a citation-archive pointer for defunct Ukrainian banks
why_relevant: Articles on failed or legacy Ukrainian banks (Finance and Credit, First Investment Bank, KredoBank, Oschadbank) systematically carry archived-URL citations with capture dates pointing at web.archive.org copies of now-dead bank pages. A cheap, high-yield way to harvest known-good archived URLs for institutions whose domains no longer resolve.

source_name: Vernadsky National Library of Ukraine — Ukrainika electronic library / e-resource archiving
why_relevant: The national library states that collecting and archiving online electronic resources is part of the Ukrainika programme — the closest thing to a national web/e-deposit archive for Ukraine. Relevant as a potential institutional custodian of pre-2022 Ukrainian corporate/official publications, though banking-sector coverage is unproven.

source_name: CS Ltd (Компанія CS) — press centre, news and customer case studies (CBS B2 core banking)
why_relevant: CS Ltd is the dominant domestic core-banking vendor in Ukraine (CBS/ABS B2, self-described #1 in Ukraine, 100+ modules). Its news and 'cases' sections name the specific banks running B2 (OTP Bank, Bank Lviv, BISbank) and announce regulatory-driven upgrades (e.g. NBU new capital-structure rules, Visa B2B Connect integration). This is the single richest indirect disclosure of which private Ukrainian banks run which core system and what capex/upgrade projects are live.

source_name: UNITY-BARS — projects / national projects and products pages (ABS BARS core banking, COPR2, Corplight)
why_relevant: Second major Ukrainian core-banking/digital-banking vendor (founded 1991, Kyiv R&D, patent holder of ABS BARS, internet/mobile banking COPR2 and Corplight, credit and DWH modules). Its 'national projects' page is an explicit customer/reference list that maps state and private institutions to specific banking platforms — a direct pointer to who runs what.

source_name: Ukrainian Processing Center (UPC / Український процесінговий центр) — corporate site and news
why_relevant: Ukraine's first and largest card processor (founded 1997, Raiffeisen Bank International group since 2005). Its announcements name the banks it processes for, the platforms it deploys (Tietoevry Card Suite), and new capabilities (open banking, cross-border acquiring). Because processing is outsourced by many private Ukrainian banks, UPC announcements reveal issuer/acquirer infrastructure choices that the banks themselves never publish.

source_name: Tietoevry Banking — newsroom press releases (Ukraine deals, Card Suite)
why_relevant: Nordic listed vendor whose regulated press releases document Ukrainian payment-infrastructure engagements with named counterparties and dates — e.g. UPC choosing Tietoevry Banking as open-banking platform partner (Mar 2023) and the earlier Tieto/UPC cross-border EU acquiring launch on Card Suite. Listed-company disclosure discipline makes these unusually reliable and dated.

source_name: Cision / news.cision.com vendor release archive (Nordic & European banking-tech vendors)
why_relevant: Press-release distribution archive that mirrors banking-tech vendor releases with stable, long-lived permalinks — useful when a vendor reorganises its own newsroom and old Ukraine deal announcements 404. Acts as an archive/aggregator pointer rather than a primary source.

source_name: UKRCARD (УКРКАРТ) — news and press releases / 'for banks' pages
why_relevant: Independent Ukrainian processing centre serving banks with debit/credit, EMV and contactless card processing. Its press releases document scheme certifications (e.g. Mastercard Automatic Billing Updater) and its 'Банки' page functions as a client list — a direct pointer to which smaller Ukrainian banks outsource processing rather than run it in-house.

source_name: ProFIX Group — payments/SWIFT integration vendor site
why_relevant: Ukrainian-rooted vendor claiming 250+ bank and financial-institution clients across 29 countries, supplying SWIFT connectivity for banks and corporates, MoneyGram services and Visa Direct Account/Wallet integration. Announcements and product pages indicate which Ukrainian banks are adding cross-border payout and SWIFT/ISO 20022 capability.

source_name: IT Ukraine Association — member directory (banking/fintech software vendors)
why_relevant: Industry-association member directory that enumerates Ukrainian IT companies with profiles and links, including banking/payments vendors such as ProFIX Group. Best used as an actor-map expander: it surfaces vendor names that then get tracked individually for bank-engagement announcements.

source_name: Prozorro public procurement portal — bank buyers (state banks) tender and award records
why_relevant: Although Ukraine's private systemic banks procure outside public tender rules, state-owned banks (PrivatBank, Oschadbank, Ukrgasbank, Sense Bank) are contracting authorities and DO publish. Observed tenders include ATM and ATM-component purchases by PrivatBank (budgets from ~1.19m to ~6.37m UAH) and acquiring/mobile POS terminal service contracts. Award records name the winning vendor, price and quantity — the hardest evidence available on payments-hardware supply in Ukraine, and a calibration baseline for inferring private-bank deals.

source_name: Prozorro mirror/aggregator marketplaces (Playtender, tender.uub.com.ua and other authorised e-platforms)
why_relevant: Authorised Prozorro e-marketplaces and tender aggregators re-index the same procurement data with friendlier category browsing (e.g. a dedicated 'Банкомати' DK021 30123200-9 category listing). Useful as a redundant access path when the central portal's search or API is rate-limited, and for category-level discovery of vendor names.

source_name: Printec Ukraine — local vendor site and corporate registry profile (ATM/POS installation and service)
why_relevant: Printec Ukraine LLC (EDRPOU 35442628, shareholder PRINTEC HOLDINGS LIMITED) supplies installation, service and repair of ATMs, POS terminals, embossers and Cisco equipment for Ukrainian banks. The local site plus the corporate-registry profile give ownership, officers and activity codes; recruitment listings independently describe the serviced device estate and service-management systems in use. Directly relevant as a competitor/peer benchmark for engagements with Ukrainian banks.

source_name: PaySpace Magazine (psm7.com) — Ukrainian fintech/payments trade press and PSM Awards
why_relevant: The principal Ukrainian trade outlet for fintech, e-commerce and payment systems. It republishes and contextualises vendor announcements about Ukrainian bank deployments, and its annual PSM Awards nomination lists are effectively a curated census of banks, payment providers, processors and technology platforms active in Ukraine — a strong actor-map and pointer source for cell #15.

source_name: FinClub (finclub.net) — Ukrainian banking/finance news
why_relevant: Specialist Ukrainian banking news service that reports vendor/infrastructure milestones which the banks do not announce themselves — e.g. UPC becoming the first Open Banking provider in Ukraine. Useful for catching vendor-bank stories that never appear in an English press release.

source_name: AIN.UA — Ukrainian tech/business outlet, banking-technology coverage
why_relevant: Covers Ukrainian bank technology adoption with dates and named parties (e.g. Sense Bank joining the Ukrainian open-banking ecosystem, Jul 2026). Complements vendor press rooms by capturing the bank-side confirmation of a vendor-announced integration.

source_name: Ukrgasbank press centre — processing/infrastructure milestone announcements
why_relevant: State-owned bank press centre that publishes infrastructure milestones a private bank would keep quiet — notably its new in-house processing passing international payment-scheme certification. Bank-side counterpart to vendor announcements; naming of scheme certifications lets you infer the platform and integrator behind a migration.

source_name: PUMB (ПУМБ) press centre and B2B acquiring pages — terminal models and acquiring supply
why_relevant: Large private Ukrainian bank whose press centre and merchant-acquiring product pages enumerate the POS device types it offers (countertop, portable, contactless, ECR-integrated, rental). Private banks rarely name suppliers, but device-model detail on acquiring pages is an indirect fingerprint of the terminal vendor behind the estate.

source_name: Checkbox / E-Chek and comparable Ukrainian PRRO+POS resellers — terminal catalogues
why_relevant: Ukrainian software-RRO (ПРРО) and terminal resellers publish concrete device catalogues and bank-acquiring partner lists, exposing which terminal hardware brands are actually distributed in Ukraine and which banks each reseller is integrated with. A practical route to the POS hardware supply chain when neither banks nor global OEMs disclose Ukrainian distributors.

source_name: Ukrainian cash-handling equipment distributors (Glory/CIMA sorters) — TCS Спецтехніка, Fintex, Eco Trading, IT-Consul, Tech Profit
why_relevant: Cash-handling is the least-disclosed segment of Ukrainian bank capex. Local distributor catalogues for Glory banknote counters/sorters (GFS-120S, GFS-220F, UW-600) and modular cash-processing and recycling systems reveal which cash-handling brands are supplied into Ukrainian banks and cash-in-transit operations, including a visible second-hand/refurbished market that signals constrained budgets.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf press releases and ATM Marketplace vendor news hub
why_relevant: ATM Marketplace maintains per-vendor news hubs for the global ATM/self-service OEMs (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR/NCR Atleos and peers), aggregating their press releases and go-live announcements. No Ukraine-specific engagement surfaced in this pass, but this is the correct standing watchpoint for the moment a global ATM OEM announces a Ukrainian bank win, and it aggregates the branch-automation/managed-services deal template these vendors use.
